answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a slow trust ramp: new identities start with no voting weight and earn it only by completing low-stakes work over weeks, like a tide that rises gradually rather than all at once. A farm spinning up thousands of copies gains nothing on day one, while a zephyr of fresh accounts cannot sway a vote before their records are checked. Copies that behave identically across the frozen tundra of transaction history cluster together and lose weight, so patience, not numbers, buys influence.
